sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the appellant/convict that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question, as there is inordinate delay of two years in lodging the First Information Report.

He submits that prosecutrix, who is aged about 17 years & 4 months at the time lodging of FIR, is consenting party to the act of the appellant, as she voluntarily eloped with the appellant and had travelled with him at various places on her own will.

He further submits that the FSL report is negative and appellant is in jail since 27.10.2020 and appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more in its final disposal, hence, he prays that the appellant be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the bail application.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties on application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail and perused the material available on record.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties, having regard to the facts & circumstances of the case,
particularly considering the fact that the there is inordinate delay of two years in lodging the FIR,
and as per statement of proseuctrix (PW-1), she voluntarily eloped with the appellant and had travelled at various places on her will; and the fact that FSL is negative; appellant is in jail since 27.10.2020 and hearing of this appeal would take prolonged period of time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He be released on bail on his executing a personal bail bond with a surety to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 18.11.2023.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, I.A. No. 1 of 2023 is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid I.A. filed in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this matter for final hearing after six weeks.
 Sd/- Sd/-
 (N.K. Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
 Judge Chief Justice Dubey/-
